notes: INSTRUMENT BALANCES NOW MEAN ONE THING: VALUE TODAY. Engine work only. The page merge, the rename to Edit balances, and removing the Instruments page are deliberately NOT in this build; they come next, so that if a figure looks wrong we know it is the maths and not the restructure. ROOT CAUSE, found in the code rather than inferred. inv.balance was documented two contradictory ways in the same file: 'current opening balances which already reflect logged tx' at the actuals overlay, and 'the horizon-start seed used to project the PAST' at applyTransactionDelta. The two sides were also asymmetric. A logged REDEMPTION reduced inv.balance; a logged CONTRIBUTION did not. The field therefore behaved as today's value when selling and as a stale historical seed when buying, so no consistent reading of the stored data was possible. The engine then seeded that figure at the horizon start and re-added every logged contribution on top, counting the same money twice. Because each page runs the projection from a different month, each page double-counted a different subset, which is why Bonds read Rs 2,00,000 on the Projection sheet and Rs 2,40,284 on Net Worth. THE FIX, IN THREE PARTS. Contributions now move the instrument balance exactly as redemptions always did, making the two symmetric. The engine anchors its series to TODAY rather than to the horizon start: months from today forward project from the stored figure, and months before it are walked BACK through logged events, which is the same pattern savings has always used. The actuals overlay no longer re-adds logged contributions, because they are already inside the balance. GROWTH IS NOT APPLIED BETWEEN EDITS, BY CHOICE. Silently compounding the stored figure would mean it is no longer the number that was typed. Contributions and redemptions are events the app observes; market movement is not. A balanceAsOf stamp is now written on every logged contribution and redemption so that staleness can be surfaced in the UI. PAST MONTHS ARE WALKED BACK WITHOUT UN-APPLYING GROWTH. Logged events are real; inferred history is not. Reconstructing a precise past value that was never recorded would be invention dressed up as data. STRESS TESTED ACROSS FIVE SCENARIOS, ALL PASSING. Logging a Rs 50,000 contribution moves the stored balance by exactly Rs 50,000 and the projection by Rs 40,000, the difference being the Rs 10,000 scheduled contribution that it absorbs. A Rs 70,000 redemption moves both by exactly minus Rs 70,000. Three instruments report identical figures whether the projection starts in May, in October, or in the current month; previously Bonds differed by Rs 40,284, FD by Rs 4,50,000 and Mutual Funds by Rs 1,79,716, with monthly-compounding instruments drifting further the longer the window. Stored balance plus this month's scheduled contribution equals the projected figure for every instrument. Closing an instrument still zeroes it from the close month. PERMANENT GUARD ADDED to the regression suite: an instrument must report the same figure whether the projection runs from the horizon start or from the sheet's window start, and the check fails loudly otherwise. Six separate implementations of shared quantities have surfaced in this codebase during this work, and an assertion is the only measure that has reliably stopped them returning. It currently reports a zero mismatch. ACTION REQUIRED BEFORE TRUSTING THE NUMBERS. Re-enter the current balance for EVERY instrument once. Contributions logged before this build were never written into the stored figures, and the engine will no longer add them on your behalf. Bonds, FD and Mutual Funds were already typed as current values and should be close. Physical gold and Stocks still hold their original May figures and will understate by the October gold purchases and the Jio IPO until re-entered. This could not be migrated automatically: distinguishing an edited balance from an untouched one is not possible from the stored data, and guessing would risk re-creating the exact double-count this build removes.
